item.title: Peoria police seek suspects in gunfire and car theft attempt
item.description: Peoria police are investigating after two ShotSpotter alerts and an alleged attempted car theft, with no injuries reported.

item.title: Peoria NAACP president honored for leadership
item.description: Pastor Marvin Hightower, the president of the NAACP Peoria, was recognized with the Jesse White Leadership award by Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs during a Black History Month celebration.

item.title: Peoria man gets 50 years behind bars for 2021 deadly shooting over $70 debt
item.description: Marvin Alexander, 24, was sentenced to 50 years in prison for the July 20, 2021, death of De'Monyae Z. Phelps, after being found guilty of shooting him over a $70 debt.

item.title: Peoria zoo celebrates tortoise's 86th birthday
item.description: George, an Aldabra tortoise at the Peoria Zoo, celebrated his 86th birthday on Wednesday, making him a wonderful ambassador for his species and a reminder that slow and steady really does win the race.

item.title: City of Peoria puts out first pollinator alert of the year
item.description: The City of Peoria has released its first Peoria Pollinator Watch of the year, highlighting the importance of small insects like woolly bear caterpillars in supporting the city's green infrastructure and improving environmental quality.

item.title: Dunlap's Wilder-Waite Elementary set for construction update
item.description: The Dunlap School District is constructing a new elementary school, Wilder-Waite Elementary, to replace the current out of date school and accommodate the influx of students, with the new school expected to open in Fall 2027.

item.title: Second Chiddix Junior High teacher on paid leave amid police investigation
item.description: A second teacher at Chiddix Junior High School has been placed on paid leave due to an investigation conducted by the Normal Police Department, with no charges or arrests made at this time.

item.title: Peoria resident shares HIV story amid high Black infection rates
item.description: According to IDPH, Black people in Illinois continue to have the highest rates of new HIV cases, despite representing only 14% of the population, and organizations led by Black people are lobbying for more state funding to help stop the spread of the virus.
